assumptions.assumption: LOWEST reads 0xFF when nothing has answered.
assumptions.reason: 0xFF cannot be a 7-bit address, so it marks "none" without another flag.

assumptions.assumption: the map has bits for all 128 addresses; reserved ones always read 0.
assumptions.reason: four aligned 32-bit words keep the address arithmetic trivial for the host.

behaviour: A write to CTRL with bit 0 = 1 while BUSY = 0 starts a scan - MAP0-MAP3 and COUNT are cleared, LOWEST is set to 0xFF, DONE is cleared and BUSY set. Writes while BUSY = 1 are ignored.
The scan probes addresses 0x08, 0x09, ... 0x77 in increasing order, one probe each - never 0x00-0x07 or 0x78-0x7F.
A probe - START, the byte {address, 0} (write), the ACK bit with SDA released (sampled at the end of its SCL high time), then STOP. No data byte is ever sent.
If the ACK bit was 0 the address answered - its MAP bit is set, COUNT increments, and LOWEST takes the address if it is the first to answer in this scan.
After the probe of 0x77 BUSY falls and DONE is set (DONE stays set until the next scan starts).
The results update during the scan, probe by probe.
Q = QUARTER clocks. Releasing SCL is followed by waiting until SCL is seen high through the two-flop synchroniser (a stretching slave holds it low); high times count from that moment.

START - SDA low, wait 2Q, SCL low, wait Q. Each of the 9 bits - set SDA (pull low for 0, release for 1), wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, sample SDA, SCL low, wait Q. STOP - SDA low, wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, release SDA, wait 2Q (bus free) before the next START.
The lines are only ever pulled low or released (high-Z).

"""Acceptance tests of t2_i2c_scanner against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from benchmark.lib.i2c_devices import Adt7420, FixedDevice, I2cBus
from model import BUSY, COUNT, CTRL, DESIGN_ID, LOWEST, MAP0, STATUS, Model

REGS = ((STATUS, "STATUS"), (COUNT, "COUNT"), (LOWEST, "LOWEST"), (MAP0, "MAP0"), (MAP0 + 1, "MAP1"),
        (MAP0 + 2, "MAP2"), (MAP0 + 3, "MAP3"))


# v1.2: SCL high time is 2Q to 2Q + SYNC_SLACK clocks. The spec says wait until SCL is seen high through a two-flop
# synchroniser, then 2Q: 2-3 clocks of synchroniser plus 1-3 of state and registered-output latency; 8 allows for that.
SYNC_SLACK = 8


class Env:
    def __init__(self, dut) -> None:
        self.b = Board(dut, {"dev_scl_pull": 0, "dev_sda_pull": 0})
        self.dut, self.m = dut, Model()
        self.q = self.b.param("QUARTER")

    async def start(self, addrs: set[int]) -> None:
        await self.b.start()
        self.bus = I2cBus(self.dut, self.devices(addrs))

    @staticmethod
    def devices(addrs: set[int]) -> list:
        return [Adt7420() if a == 0x4B else FixedDevice(a) for a in sorted(addrs)]

    async def regs(self) -> None:
        for off, name in REGS:
            await self.b.expect(off, self.m.read(off), name)
        led = await peek(self.b.clk, self.dut.LED)
        assert led == self.m.leds(), f"LED {led:#x} != model {self.m.leds():#x}"

    async def scan(self, addrs: set[int]) -> None:
        self.bus.clear()
        self.bus.addr_probes.clear()
        await self.b.write(CTRL, 1)
        want = self.m.scan({a for a in addrs if 0x08 <= a <= 0x77})
        for _ in range(200):
            await self.b.cycles(2000)
            if not (await self.b.read(STATUS)) & BUSY:
                break
        assert not self.bus.errors, self.bus.errors[:3]
        assert self.bus.addr_probes == list(range(0x08, 0x78)), f"probed {[hex(a) for a in self.bus.addr_probes][:12]}..."
        assert self.bus.log == want, "bus log differs from the model (first difference at entry " \
            f"{next((i for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(self.bus.log, want)) if x != y), min(len(self.bus.log), len(want)))})"
        await self.regs()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1268680, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(set())
    assert await e.b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    await e.regs()
    for off in (CTRL, 0x08, 0x7F):
        await e.b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped / write-only")
    assert int(dut.scl.value) == 1 and int(dut.sda.value) == 1, "bus not released after reset"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1581910, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_scan_finds_devices(dut):
    present = {0x03, 0x08, 0x1D, 0x4B, 0x77, 0x7A}       # 0x03 and 0x7A are reserved: never probed
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(present)
    await e.scan(present)
    assert e.bus.devices[3].writes == [], "a data byte reached the ADT7420"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1581890, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_empty_bus(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(set())
    await e.scan(set())


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=2333010, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_rescan_clears_and_busy(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start({0x20, 0x21, 0x5F})
    await e.scan({0x20, 0x21, 0x5F})
    e.bus.devices = Env.devices({0x4B, 0x60})
    e.bus.clear()
    e.bus.addr_probes.clear()
    await e.b.write(CTRL, 1)
    await e.b.cycles(3000)
    assert (await e.b.read(STATUS)) & BUSY, "not busy during a scan"
    await e.b.expect(COUNT, 0, "COUNT early in the new scan (cleared, nothing found yet)")
    await e.b.expect(MAP0 + 1, 0, "MAP1 cleared by the new scan")
    await e.b.write(CTRL, 1)                         # ignored while busy: the scan does not restart
    want = e.m.scan({0x4B, 0x60})
    for _ in range(200):
        await e.b.cycles(2000)
        if not (await e.b.read(STATUS)) & BUSY:
            break
    assert e.bus.addr_probes == list(range(0x08, 0x78)), "a write while busy restarted or disturbed the scan"
    assert e.bus.log == want
    await e.regs()
    await e.b.write(CTRL, 0)                         # bit 0 clear: no scan
    await e.b.cycles(500)
    await e.regs()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1581890, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_clock_stretching_and_timing(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start({0x4B})
    e.bus.stretch_next = 400                         # the sensor stretches SCL after its ACK
    await e.scan({0x4B})
    hi, lo = 2 * e.q, 2 * e.q
    assert all(hi <= h <= hi + SYNC_SLACK for h in e.bus.high), f"SCL high times {sorted(set(e.bus.high))}, 2Q = {hi}"
    assert all(lo <= t <= lo + 2 for t in e.bus.low), f"SCL low times {sorted(set(e.bus.low))}, 2Q = {lo}"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=2163470, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_random_population(dut):
    rng = random.Random(int(cocotb.RANDOM_SEED))
    present = set(rng.sample(range(0x00, 0x80), 9)) | {0x4B}
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(present)
    await e.scan(present)
    present2 = set(rng.sample(range(0x08, 0x78), 3))
    e.bus.devices = Env.devices(present2)
    await e.scan(present2)

requirements.text: A scan probes exactly 0x08-0x77 in order, each with START, a write address, the ACK bit and STOP, and no data byte
MAP, COUNT, LOWEST and DONE report the addresses that ACKed; a new scan clears them first
Clock stretching is honoured and the lines are never driven high
On the board the scan finds the ADT7420 at 0x4B
The design closes timing at 100 MHz with no unconstrained path

resources_expected: a couple of hundred LUTs and FFs (the 112-bit map in flops); no BRAM, no DSP
spec_md:
# I2C bus scanner on the temperature-sensor bus

I'd like a small I2C bus scanner on the Nexys A7-100T's sensor bus (TMP_SCL / TMP_SDA), like the "i2cdetect"
tool, so I can see what answers.

- When I tell it to start, it probes every normal 7-bit address from 0x08 to 0x77 in turn: a write-address probe,
  check for the ACK, then a STOP, and on to the next. The reserved addresses at both ends are left alone, and it
  must never send a data byte to anything.
- Results: a 128-bit map with one bit per address, how many answered, the lowest address that answered, and busy /
  done flags. A new scan starts from a clean map.
- The LEDs show how many devices answered.
- Open-drain lines with the board's pull-ups (never drive them high); a slave may stretch the clock.
- SCL speed from a parameter giving a quarter of the SCL period in clocks; 100 kHz on the board.
- Through the test shell; design ID "SCAN".

Test hooks: top module `t2_i2c_scanner_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC (`TMP_SCL`, `TMP_SDA`, `LED`,
the USB-UART pins, `CLK100MHZ`, `CPU_RESETN`), the test shell's `CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP`
parameters, plus `QUARTER` (a quarter of the SCL period, in clocks) as top-level parameters.
title: I2C bus scanner on the temperature-sensor bus

Probe 0x09: START, address byte 0x12 (write), then STOP; no answer (ACK bit left high).

trace.stimulus: A scan is started over a bus where the devices at 0x1d, 0x4b answer. Only the probes of 0x08 to 0x0a, 0x1a to 0x20, 0x48 to 0x4d are shown (the rest of the scan runs the same way); every probe is a write address and a STOP, never a data byte.

what: A bus scanner in the style of the i2cdetect tool. When started, it tries every normal seven-bit I2C address in turn by sending the address with a write request, checking whether anything acknowledges, and then sending a stop. It never sends a data byte. The results are a map with one bit per address, a count of devices that answered, the lowest address that answered, and busy and done flags, and the LEDs show the count.
where: Scanning is the first step when bringing up a board with unknown or mis-wired I2C parts, and the same probe appears in operating-system tools and in firmware that detects which optional chips are fitted.
